newsitem.title: UK: NatWest, Tesco discuss agreement end.
newsitem.headline: NatWest, Tesco discuss agreement end.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc would push for compensation from Tesco Plc if current discussions on ending an agreement to run the supermarket's ClubCard Plus interest-paying account result in any costs, the bank said on Tuesday.

NatWest chairman Lord Alexander told a news conference after the bank reported year pretax profits of 1.12 billion pounds that the bank is discussing the termination of the contract with Tesco and has taken legal advice.

"If there are costs from the end of the contract we will have to discuss that with Tesco," Alexander said but added that the amount would not be material and that NatWest is still very much involved with Tesco.
A spokeswoman for Tesco said there had been no breach of contract by either party and "no animosity."
She added that Tesco had asked NatWest to join them as Tesco expanded further into financial services but the bank had said it "didn't share the same vision."
Tesco switched to a joint venture with Royal Bank of Scotland earlier this month, which will take over ClubCard Plus and launch a credit card over the summer.
Tesco initially teamed up with NatWest for ClubCard Plus in mid-1996.
